Claude Code: Use the agent-loop commands (/goal, /ultra-plan) to let Claude run autonomously for hours instead of babysitting each step - it saves credits by avoiding repeated re-prompting.
Install MCP servers (Perplexity, Playwright, Firecrawl, Chrome) to give Claude Code live internet, browser control and site-crawling.
Run Rufflow to spin up 60+ specialized agents (queen + workers) that share memory and auto-route tasks by complexity.
Add the UI/UX Pro Max design skill so Claude reasons about layout instead of guessing.
Claude: Add Nano Banana as a Claude skill plus a Google AI Studio API key to generate and edit images from chat with /banana.
Add custom connectors via Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector to pull external data (e.g., Viralo trends) into Claude.
Claude Design's prototype mode can make motion graphics, but there's no MP4 export yet - screen-record for now.
Cursor: Cursor Composer 2.5 runs about 14x cheaper per task than Opus while staying competitive on coding benchmarks - use it for high-volume agentic coding.
Manus AI: Give Manus a goal and it opens tabs, clicks, fills forms and sends emails autonomously, like a digital employee.
It's strong for lead-gen scraping and wide research with zero code.
Base 44: Describe the app you want and Base 44 scaffolds the whole thing - landing page, pricing and checkout included.

prompt engineering: Use a reasoning/UX skill layer (e.g., UI/UX Pro Max) so the model reasons about design choices instead of guessing.
automation: Loop an agent against a written goal so it self-checks and keeps working until the goal is met, even for hours.
Pair a design/image model (Nano Banana 2) with a one-click deploy (Vercel) to ship sites fast.
agents: Queen/worker agent swarms with shared memory outperform a single agent and auto-route subtasks by complexity.
Model-agnostic agents (e.g., Goose) avoid vendor lock-in by swapping between Claude, GPT, Gemini and DeepSeek.
Agentic 'digital employees' can run full web workflows - browsing, forms, email - unattended.
code: The harness (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) matters as much as the model - a cheaper model in a better harness can win.
No-code AI app builders (Base 44) can ship a sellable MVP, including payments, without writing code.
parallel tasks: Spin up background/parallel agent sessions (/agents) so multiple tasks run at once.
self-improving systems: Build an 'improve system' skill with modes (audit, skill review, historical review) so your agent upgrades its own skills over time.
Clone domain experts into an 'ask the board' panel the agent consults before acting.
harness code: Benchmarks like Cursor Bench, SWE-bench multilingual and Terminal Bench compare coding agents across harnesses, not just raw models.
